   210	---
   211	
   212	# Ocean Leptos/WASM Surface
   213	
   214	## Overview
   215	
   216	Ocean is a **native instrument panel molded from dark water**, not an AI landing page and not a control-heavy developer dashboard. The stage is almost black. Familiar product controls feel machined into it: raised controls catch one restrained overhead highlight; inputs and code wells recede into depth; active agent work appears as faint bioluminescence.
   217	
   218	The product register is trusted desktop software in the lineage of Linear, Figma, and Raycast: compact, direct, readable, and unsurprising. Ocean retains its own identity through the deep-indigo-to-bright-aqua depth ramp and the circular wave coin. It does not copy those products' chrome.
   219	
   220	The same Leptos/WASM product core renders browser, PWA, Chrome side panel, Tauri desktop, and future mobile shells. A shell may add platform capability, but it must not invent a second visual language.
   221	
   222	**Control density is a design defect.** Show the control needed now. Put secondary actions behind one overflow, reveal power controls on intent, and remove unavailable capabilities instead of rendering dead chrome. One primary action should dominate any local decision.
   223	
   224	## Colors
   225	
   226	### The dark stage
   227	
   228	- **Background `{colors.background}`** is the page and deepest transcript void.
   229	- **Raised `{colors.surface-raised}`** is for bars, assistant surfaces, and drawers.
   230	- **Elevated `{colors.surface-elevated}`** is for cards, controls, chips, and docks.
   231	- **Hover `{colors.surface-hover}`** is a temporary interaction state, never a permanent panel color.
   232	- **Well `{colors.surface-well}`** is reserved for code, diffs, terminal-like data, and inset transcript bodies.
   233	
   234	Text steps down deliberately: `{colors.text-primary}` for headings and decisive content, `{colors.text-secondary}` for readable body copy, `{colors.text-metadata}` for labels and context, and `{colors.text-disabled}` only for disabled content. Never use disabled grey for ordinary readable copy.
   235	
   236	### The OCEAN depth ramp
   237	
   238	The identity ramp rises from abyss to surface:
   239	
   240	`{colors.ocean-1}` → `{colors.ocean-2}` → `{colors.ocean-3}` → `{colors.ocean-4}` → `{colors.ocean-5}` → `{colors.ocean-6}` → `{colors.ocean-7}` → `{colors.ocean-8}`.
   241	
   242	Use these as **solid colors on discrete identity elements**: individual wordmark letters, banner rows, chart segments, or vector layers inside the mark. Never gradient-clip text. A continuous OCEAN-ramp color gradient is permitted only inside data visualization or the circular mark, never on a button. Neutral low-alpha material sheens are allowed on raised surfaces because they describe overhead light rather than brand color.
   243	
   244	`{colors.primary}` is the working interactive cyan. It appears only on:
   245	
   246	1. the single primary action in a decision,
   247	2. focus indication,
   248	3. live/recording or an explicit live-attention state,
   249	4. concise active selection cues.
   250	
   251	Ordinary in-flight tool work is amber `{colors.status-warning}`. The Dynamic Island may use primary cyan for running because it is explicitly a live attention surface; this is a named exception, not the generic running color.
   252	
   253	Accent-filled controls always use dark ink `{colors.on-primary}`, never white.
   254	
   255	### Badge-confined material palette
   256	
   257	`badge-face`, `badge-rim`, `badge-band-1` through `badge-band-6`, `badge-foam`, `badge-split`, and `badge-gloss` are scoped material-reference tokens from the live badge system. They describe the intended muted turquoise-to-indigo family but are **not sufficient to reconstruct the production logo**: the packaged PNG/SVG contain the authoritative static geometry and embedded paints, while the live Canvas tide coin uses its own rendered water material. These tokens are not a second UI palette and are not permission to spread teal through navigation or controls.
   258	
   259	### Semantic state
   260	
   261	- Connected, completed, and valid: `{colors.status-success}`.
   262	- Running, reconnecting, pending permission, and caution: `{colors.status-warning}` unless an explicitly live action uses primary cyan.
   263	- Failed, destructive, denied, and barge/error state: `{colors.status-error}`.
   264	- Informational headings and neutral system context: `{colors.status-info}`.
   265	- Live participation is primary cyan, not conventional recording red.
   266	
   267	Use soft semantic backgrounds only as quiet tints. Do not turn status into colored slabs.
   268	
   269	## Typography
   270	
   271	Poppins is the product voice. It should feel compact and engineered, not promotional.
   272	
   273	- **Display and title** are modest: 22px and 18px, semibold. There are no giant hero headlines in the product.
   274	- **Body** is 14px/1.55. Assistant prose may open to 1.6 line-height for sustained reading.
   275	- **Secondary and small** copy are 13px and 12px.
   276	- **Labels** are 11px semibold uppercase with `0.08em` tracking. Use this register for table headers, filenames, and small section labels—not whole paragraphs.
   277	- **Metadata** is quiet 11px text. Paths, IDs, token counts, numbers, code, and technical values use the data face.
   278	- **Mono is for data, never for ordinary UI labels.** Use the platform stack `ui-monospace, "SF Mono", SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace` in implementation.
   279	- **Wordmark** letters are separately filled Poppins Bold characters. The current uppercase lockup uses 14px with `0.22em` tracking; mark-only, lowercase, and tighter uppercase lockups remain review variants rather than three canonical logos.
   280	
   281	Use weight and contrast before introducing another size. A view should rarely need more than three type levels at once.
   282	
   283	## Layout
   284	
   285	The desktop product shell is centered at a maximum width of **1120px**. It becomes full width in narrow and extension contexts. Preserve viewport safe areas and a true full-height chain.
   286	
   287	### Core geometry
   288	
   289	- Header: 56px minimum height, 16px horizontal padding, 8px control gaps.
   290	- Standard control: 34px high. Compact control: 28px high.
   291	- Transcript: roughly 72ch prose measure; 18px vertical rhythm; readable edge gutters.
   292	- Composer: one two-row dock. The chromeless textarea owns row one. Voice, quiet turn controls, and one Send/Stop slot share row two.
   293	- Composer textarea: 32px minimum writing row, growing upward to 240px.
   294	- Workspace: transcript remains the center of record; desktop workbench modules reveal only when useful.
   295	
   296	Use the 4/8/12/16/24/32/48 spacing scale. Vary rhythm by relationship; do not put 12px around everything.
   297	
   298	### Responsive posture
   299	
   300	At 720px and below, preserve one header row. Remove token metadata, collapse labels to state dots when necessary, shorten controls, and keep the transcript readable. At 480px and below, components genuinely reflow: kanban columns stack, tables become labeled row cards, charts wrap, dashboards and stats become one column, and confirm actions wrap.
   301	
   302	The Chrome side panel always uses the compact posture. Mobile is not a later redesign; compact.css is the mobile grammar. No essential action may depend on hover.
   303	
   304	## Elevation & Depth
   305	
   306	Ocean material uses one overhead light.
   307	
   308	- **Raised level 1:** controls, menu rows, chips, and compact session rows. A faint top-edge specular plus a tight dark drop.
   309	- **Raised level 2:** cards, composer dock, list panels, and substantial components.
   310	- **Raised level 3:** popovers, modals, tooltips, and the expanded Dynamic Island.
   311	- **Carved well:** inputs, code, diffs, and data bodies use an inset shadow on `{colors.surface-well}`.
   312	- **Pressed:** a raised control moves down 1px and replaces its lift with an inset shadow.
   313	
   314	An element takes a border recipe **or** an elevation recipe. Never combine a one-pixel border with a large soft shadow. Hairlines may define a flat transcript boundary, but they must not become glowing card outlines.
   315	
   316	Glow is state, not decoration. Thinking receives a faint cognition bloom; streaming may breathe a subtle aqua specular; live voice may use a stronger brand glow. Idle surfaces do not glow.
   317	
   318	Motion is quick and tidal: 160ms feedback, 240ms standard transitions, and 420ms deliberate overlay movement. Overlays may rise 8px from depth. Nothing bounces, overshoots, or performs a decorative page-load entrance. Every animation has a static reduced-motion treatment.
   319	
   320	## Shapes
   321	
   322	The shape language is compact and machined:
   323	
   324	- 4px for chips, badges, tabs, and menu rows.
   325	- 6px for controls, inputs, selects, list rows, and menus.
   326	- 10px for true cards, panels, modals, and the composer dock.
   327	- 999px only for physical geometry: circles, status dots, the voice orb, progress tracks, and scrollbar thumbs.
   328	
   329	Text-bearing pill controls are prohibited. Cards and inputs never exceed 16px radius. Do not nest cards. A component that already sits inside an assistant reply card should flatten its outer frame and preserve only meaningful inner wells.
   330	
   331	The circular Ocean mark is an intentional identity object, not a precedent for circular navigation chrome.
   332	
   333	## Components
   334	
   335	### Primary, secondary, ghost, and danger controls
   336	
   337	A primary button is compact, content-width, solid `{colors.primary}`, and set in dark `{colors.on-primary}` ink at semibold weight. It is 34px high with `0 14px` implementation padding. Hover brightens slightly; press is a restrained 1px depression. Never create a full-width cyan slab.
   338	
   339	Secondary controls use neutral elevated material. Ghost controls are transparent and metadata-grey until hover/focus. Danger controls retain the secondary shape and use error text with an error-soft hover. Approve follows primary; deny and stop follow danger.
   340	
   341	### Inputs and selects
   342	
   343	Inputs are quiet carved or raised dark fields with primary text and metadata-grey placeholders. Focus uses one cyan ring. Selects use the same shape and a custom neutral chevron; they are sans-serif controls, not mono data chips.
   344	
   345	The main composer is the exception: the textarea is chromeless because the composer dock is already the frame. The dock owns `focus-within`.
   346	
   347	### Header and overflow
   348	
   349	The header shows identity, current project/session context, one Sessions affordance, terse runtime state, and one overflow. Secondary actions—Council, Rooms, mute, capture, and comparable host features—belong in the overflow or disappear when unavailable.
   350	
   351	The overflow reference is a plain elevated menu: tight 6px radius, 4px inset, 13px rows, no icon-title-subtitle lockups, and no accent chrome.
   352	
   353	### Transcript
   354	
   355	User input is a compact raised card aligned to the right. Assistant output is a single readable response surface aligned left. Do not create a bubble around every paragraph or component.
   356	
   357	Thinking is quiet and italic. Tool activity is a mono disclosure row with a tiny status dot and a locally scrolling well when expanded. Running is amber; success is green; failure is red. Full error payloads belong in expanded transcript detail, while the global status remains one concise recoverable line.
   358	
   359	### Rich agent components
   360	
   361	Tables, kanban, charts, forms, progress, dashboards, timelines, stats, file trees, code, diffs, galleries, confirmations, maps, and video are data-first. Use 11px label headings, 12/13px content, mono numerals, hairline separators, and hover only on interactive rows. Code and diff bodies are wells; additions and deletions use semantic tints rather than neon rails.
   362	
   363	Do not generate uniform icon-heading-description component grids. A component exists to carry data or action, not to advertise a capability.
   364	
   365	### Permissions
   366	
   367	A permission request is a compact elevated decision surface with a short label, tool name, plain-language reason, lossless args in a data well, and exactly two actions: deny and approve. The pending state may use an amber ring or tint. Preserve keyboard focus and the ability to recover from failure.
   368	
   369	### Composer and voice
   370	
   371	The composer is one dock with one action slot. Send and Stop are mutually exclusive. Voice is neutral when idle, cyan when live/capturing, amber when transcribing, and quiet/static when off. The settings trigger keeps a visible floor on touch. A full realtime voice state may promote the orb, but it must yield when the agent renders useful content.
   372	
   373	### Dynamic Island
   374	
   375	The Tauri Island is a living attention object, not a dashboard. Compact form shows the focused session and a tiny state cue. Expanded form replaces itself with exactly one mode at a time: Agent, Sessions, or Recall. It does not append heterogeneous feeds. Running uses cyan, needs-human uses amber, failure uses red, and healthy idle uses a quiet green cue.
   376	
   377	### Panels and overlays
   378	
   379	Sessions is a centered modal; Rooms is a right slide-over. Both use the same row vocabulary and conditional action disclosure. Overlay blur belongs only to the backdrop. Destructive row actions reveal on hover, focus, or a clear tap path.
   380	
   381	## Do's and Don'ts
   382	
   383	### Do
   384	
   385	- Use near-black neutral surfaces and ration the OCEAN ramp to identity and state.
   386	- Use `{colors.on-primary}` on cyan fills.
   387	- Show one primary action and move secondary actions behind one overflow.
   388	- Prefer conditional rendering and reveal-on-intent to permanent controls.
   389	- Keep error summaries short, truthful, and recoverable.
   390	- Use solid ramp colors on discrete letters, rows, layers, or data marks.
   391	- Design desktop and compact behavior in the same component pass.
   392	- Preserve visible focus, touch paths, safe areas, and reduced-motion alternatives.
   393	- Use the existing 24×24 round-stroke icon family and real service marks when necessary.
   394	- Validate components in the 380px side panel, at ≤480px, and on the 1120px desktop shell.
   395	
   396	### Don't
   397	
   398	- Don't use magenta or purple, legacy mint `#7FE7C8`, or navy `#06111D` chrome.
   399	- Don't use gradient-clipped text, gradient buttons, or white text on cyan.
   400	- Don't use terminal prompts, cursors, underscores, brackets, sparkles, stars, mascots, or generic AI magic as Ocean identity.
   401	- Don't use pill-shaped text controls, nested cards, full-width accent slabs, or accent scrollbars.
   402	- Don't use glassmorphism as the default material.
   403	- Don't combine a one-pixel border with a broad blurred shadow.
   404	- Don't build icon-title-subtitle launcher grids or permanent same-weight action rows.
   405	- Don't hide an essential action behind hover on touch devices.
   406	- Don't redraw the canonical logo from prose or accept generated typography as a production wordmark.
   407	
   408	## Identity and Logo
   409	
   410	The production identity input is `assets/master-1024.png`; `assets/ocean-mark.svg` is the portable vector. Treat their silhouette, circular rim, wave spacing, depth order, internal cutouts, and embedded static colors as immutable. The static mark and the live Canvas tide coin belong to one identity family, but only the checked-in static files are production logo sources. Do not rebuild the static logo from the front-matter badge or water tokens.
   411	
   412	The badge is a matte near-black coin with shallow rim relief and stacked water depth. It is not a glossy SaaS orb, a photoreal ocean, or a cyberpunk neon emblem. The rim remains calm while loading motion moves water inside the clip.
   413	
   414	Mark-only is production-safe. Lowercase `ocean` and uppercase `OCEAN` lockups remain visual review variants. Clear space, legal usage, monochrome/light variants, and minimum reproduction size are not yet canonical; do not invent them.
   415	
   416	## Iconography
   417	
   418	Product icons use a 24×24 viewBox, 2px optical stroke, round caps, round joins, `currentColor`, and a restrained outline vocabulary. They should remain legible at 16, 20, and 24px. Filled geometry is reserved for inherently filled concepts such as Stop or an official service mark.
   419	
   420	Prioritize literal product concepts: Sessions, Recall, permission, needs reply, browser driving, file, editor, repo branch, diff, checks, artifact, call, voice state, Council, Canvas, and host capability. Do not create a separate illustrative icon family and do not use emoji in product UI.
   421	
   422	Every custom icon delivery should include:
   423	
   424	- optimized SVG with no embedded text or raster,
   425	- 24×24 master geometry,
   426	- 16/20/24/32px contact sheet,
   427	- dark-stage and one-color previews,
   428	- `currentColor` version,
   429	- short semantic name and accessibility label,
   430	- no baked shadow or glow.
   431	
   432	## Motion and State
   433	
   434	Use motion only to clarify state change:
   435	
   436	- Hover/focus/press: 160ms.
   437	- Standard component transition: 240ms.
   438	- Overlay or tidal rise: 420ms maximum.
   439	- New streamed content: opacity plus 2px rise.
   440	- Loading mark: internal wave shear/drift; calm rim; never spin.
   441	- Permission wait: amber ring pulse.
   442	- Live: cyan dot pulse.
   443	- Connected: green.
   444	- Reconnecting/running: amber unless the action is explicitly live.
   445	- Failure/barge: red.
   446	
   447	Reduced motion removes looping movement, transforms, and animated entrances while preserving state through color, copy, and static geometry.
   448	
   449	## Responsive and Accessibility
   450	
   451	A missing host capability renders as absence, not an error. Every hover reveal has a keyboard and touch path. All icon-only controls require an accessible name. Status updates use a live region without flooding it with tool output. Decorative logo layers are hidden from assistive technology while the product name remains available as text.
   452	
   453	Maintain WCAG AA for ordinary text. Metadata may be quieter but must remain readable. Never rely on hue alone: state combines color with a dot, label, icon, or action. Preserve IME composition, keyboard navigation, Escape dismissal, and sensible focus return.
   454	
   455	## AI Asset Generation Brief
   456	
   457	Use image generation for **exploratory supporting assets, icon concept sheets, component mood studies, and non-logo backgrounds**. Do not use it to redraw the production logo or typeset a final wordmark.
   458	
   459	Every prompt must state:
   460	

--- STAGED ---

--- DESIGN FILES ---
design-systems/ocean-leptos/assets/master-1024.png
design-systems/ocean-leptos/assets/ocean-mark.svg
design-systems/ocean-leptos/DESIGN.md

## Review

**Not clean. Re-review required.**

- **Blocker (high): canonical badge palette is factually misleading.** `design-systems/ocean-leptos/DESIGN.md:40-53,253-255` says the badge-band tokens create the production mark and its animation. The packaged SVG instead uses different literal colors (`design-systems/ocean-leptos/assets/ocean-mark.svg:5-37`), while the current Canvas Tide Coin hardcodes another palette (`crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/icons.rs:24-28,64-77,107-155`). **Smallest safe fix:** declare `assets/master-1024.png` and `assets/ocean-mark.svg` the sole static-logo color/geometry authority; describe `water-*` separately as live Tide Coin material; remove or clearly mark `badge-band-*` as non-reconstructive reference tokens.

- **Blocker (high): primary-button YAML contradicts the canonical control recipe.** `DESIGN.md:122-128` references `{typography.secondary}`, which is weight 400 at `DESIGN.md:75-79`, while the prose requires semibold at `DESIGN.md:335` and the binding recipe requires 13px/600 with `padding: 0 14px` (`docs/OCEAN_WEB_SURFACE_DESIGN.md:149-152`). Scalar `padding: 14px` also conflicts with a 34px control height. **Smallest safe fix:** add a 13px/600 control-label typography token and use it for the primary button; encode schema-valid horizontal padding such as `"0px 14px"` or omit padding from YAML and retain it in prose.

- **Important (medium): running-state color rules contradict one another.** `DESIGN.md:244-249` broadly assigns primary cyan to running, while `DESIGN.md:259-260,442` and `styles/tokens.css:112-116` assign ordinary running/in-flight work amber. The Dynamic Island intentionally uses cyan (`DESIGN.md:371-373`; `styles/island.css:84-89,630-632`). **Smallest safe fix:** remove generic “running” from the primary-cyan list and identify Dynamic Island running as the explicit live-attention exception.

- **Important (medium): the copy-ready prompts do not satisfy their own prompt checklist.** `DESIGN.md:457-465` requires every prompt to specify target shell, exact canvas/alpha, hard negatives, and source/export deliverables. The icon prompt at `DESIGN.md:469-471` lacks target shell and overall canvas dimensions; the component prompt at `DESIGN.md:473-475` lacks exact canvas/alpha/export requirements and omits WCAG/non-color state cues plus several hard brand negatives. The supporting prompt’s “layered source” request at `DESIGN.md:477-479` is not a reliable ChatGPT image-generation deliverable. **Smallest safe fix:** add shell/canvas/alpha placeholders, WCAG AA and non-hue state requirements, the full purple/magenta/mint/gradient-text/terminal-symbol negatives, and request a clean raster plus reconstruction/layer map unless a layered design tool is explicitly used.

- **Important (medium): the gradient prohibition is overbroad relative to the shipped material system.** `DESIGN.md:242` permits continuous gradients only in data visualization or the mark, but neutral overhead-light sheens are canonical tokens (`styles/tokens.css:149-153`) and are used on transcript surfaces (`styles/transcript.css:349-370,411-417`). **Smallest safe fix:** qualify the prohibition as applying to continuous **OCEAN-ramp/color** gradients, while explicitly permitting neutral specular material sheens.

- **Minor (low): the YAML mono family is not cross-platform.** `DESIGN.md:96-100` specifies only `"SF Mono"`, despite the prose at `DESIGN.md:275-276` and source token at `styles/tokens.css:123-125` requiring the platform fallback stack. **Smallest safe fix:** use `ui-monospace, "SF Mono", SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace` in the YAML token.

- **Medium — Resolve cross-system semantic-token drift.** `ocean-leptos/DESIGN.md:7-9` defines `on-primary: #03181A` and `primary-deep: #0087AF`, while `ocean-tui/DESIGN.md:7-8` gives the same names `#060606` and `#005FAF`. The TUI values are undocumented and unused. Align shared tokens or rename the TUI-specific deep-logo role and explain the mapping.

- **Medium — Correct the TUI thinking-state claim.** `ocean-tui/DESIGN.md:195,397` says thinking currently uses violet. The active renderer uses muted `theme::COMMENT` for thinking (`../ocean-os/crates/ocean-tui/src/shell/components/chat.rs:3191-3194`); violet is used for Graph/config accents. Either describe violet thinking as proposed or document the current muted treatment.

- **Medium — Make the “copy-ready” image prompts satisfy their own output contract.** The Leptos contract requires canvas, alpha, exact state colors, and deliverables at `ocean-leptos/DESIGN.md:457-465`, but the component prompt at `:475` omits exact canvas/alpha/export details and semantic success/warning/error colors. The TUI component prompt at `ocean-tui/DESIGN.md:436` likewise requests running/error states without supplying their token values. Add explicit placeholders for pixel dimensions, transparency/background, formats/source, and all requested state colors.

- **Low — Triage and justify packaged lint warnings.** The bundled reports still contain 34 and 18 warnings (`ocean-leptos/lint-report.json:178-181`, `ocean-tui/lint-report.json:98-101`). Some identify genuinely ambiguous tokens: Leptos water colors are undocumented and unused (`ocean-leptos/DESIGN.md:51-53`), while TUI defines an unused shadow token despite prohibiting shadows (`ocean-tui/DESIGN.md:24,266,355`). 455	## AI Asset Generation Brief
   456	
   457	Use image generation for **exploratory supporting assets, icon concept sheets, component mood studies, and non-logo backgrounds**. Do not use it to redraw the production logo or typeset a final wordmark.
   458	
   459	Every prompt must state:
   460	
   461	1. the asset role and target shell,
   462	2. exact canvas and alpha requirement,
   463	3. the attached canonical mark as immutable when present,
   464	4. exact token names and hex values,
   465	5. the one-overhead-light material model,
   466	6. hard negative constraints,
   467	7. source and export deliverables.
   468	
   469	For production logo-bearing outputs, composite `assets/master-1024.png` or `assets/ocean-mark.svg` deterministically after generation. Do not trust generated edges, text, or wave geometry.
   470	
   471	### Copy-ready custom icon prompt
   472	
   473	> Design a coherent set of **[N] Ocean product icons** for **[features]** on the **[web / PWA / extension / Tauri / mobile]** shell. Use a 24×24 master grid on a **[pixel dimensions]** transparent RGBA canvas, 2px monoline strokes, round caps and joins, flat orthographic geometry, and one-color `currentColor` output. The set must read clearly at 16px and match serious native productivity software. Use no text, letters, emoji, purple, magenta, mint chrome, gradient-clipped text, sparkles, stars, mascots, terminal prompts, cursors, brackets, baked shadows, or decorative waves. Ocean identity comes from the product, not from putting a wave in every icon. Deliver individual SVG reconstruction paths, transparent PNG previews, and a 16/20/24/32px contact sheet on `{colors.background}` `#060606`.
   474	
   475	### Copy-ready component exploration prompt
   476	
   477	> Create a high-fidelity **[pixel dimensions]** opaque component study for the **Ocean Leptos/WASM [web / extension / Tauri / mobile] surface**: **[component]** in idle, hover, focus, active, disabled, running, success, warning, and error states. Use `{colors.background}` `#060606`, `{colors.surface-raised}` `#0A0A0A`, `{colors.surface-elevated}` `#141414`, `{colors.text-primary}` `#FAFCFF`, `{colors.text-secondary}` `#B8B9BB`, scarce `{colors.primary}` `#00D7D7` with dark `{colors.on-primary}` `#03181A`, success `{colors.status-success}` `#1ED760`, warning `{colors.status-warning}` `#FFB224`, and error `{colors.status-error}` `#FF4D67`. Poppins, compact 34px controls, 6px control radius, one overhead specular, carved wells, WCAG AA text contrast, and a non-color cue for every state. No purple, magenta, mint chrome, gradient-clipped text, terminal symbols, glassmorphism, pill text controls, nested cards, gradient buttons, giant blur shadows, sparkles, mascots, or generic AI ornament. Show desktop and 380px compact layouts with equivalent hierarchy. Deliver an opaque PNG study plus a reconstruction spec listing tokens, dimensions, spacing, and state behavior.
   478	
   479	### Copy-ready supporting asset prompt
   480	
   481	> Create a **[asset role]** for Ocean **[surface]** at **[dimensions]**. Use the attached `master-1024.png` as an immutable brand mark: preserve its exact circular silhouette, rim, stacked wave spacing, internal depth, and embedded colors; do not redraw or reinterpret it. Stage on **[transparent RGBA / opaque #060606]** with **[safe zone]**. Material is matte near-black with shallow overhead relief and restrained shadow. Use only **[token names + hex values]**. No generated text, watermark, purple, magenta, mint chrome, gradient-clipped text, white-on-cyan controls, terminal/code/cursor/bracket symbols, sparkle/star motifs, mascots, glassmorphism, cyberpunk neon, lens flare, extra rings, or extra wave bands. Deliver a clean PNG/SVG-ready concept, alpha preview, contact sheet at target sizes, and a reconstruction/layer map; request a native layered source only when the selected design tool supports one.
   482	
   483	## Asset Delivery and QA
   484	
   485	The package should preserve a transparent 1024×1024 source, optimized SVG where applicable, and explicit opaque platform exports. Review every icon-like output at 16, 20, 24, 32, 48, 192, and 512px on transparent and `{colors.background}` stages. Check alpha halos, one-color legibility, compact-width behavior, touch affordances, and reduced-motion fallback.
   486	
   487	Record model, version, prompt, generation ID or seed, and post-processing steps. Generated output remains a proposal until reviewed against this DESIGN.md and the canonical assets.

}
